questions.question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct meaning of the idiom.
Blue code of silence.

options.text: An absence of speech or sound that creates or communicates an especially effective or poignant message
An unspoken policy or concealment by police regarding the wrongdoing or illicit activity of other officers.
A very tense, awkward, or uncomfortable atmosphere among a group of people

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option (3)'** i.e. **'An unspoken policy or concealment by police regarding the wrongdoing or illicit activity of other officers.'**.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **'Blue code of silence'** refers to a custom or unwritten rule among **police officers** where they refuse to report or testify against their colleagues for any **misconduct** or **criminal activity**. (पुलिस अधिकारियों के बीच अपने सहयोगियों के गलत कामों की रिपोर्ट न करने की एक अघोषित नीति)
 
 
• **Example: **The internal investigation was hampered by the **blue code of silence**, as no officer was willing to speak against their partner.
 
 
 
• **'An unspoken policy or concealment by police regarding the wrongdoing or illicit activity of other officers'** describes the systemic culture of protecting fellow law enforcement members from legal or disciplinary consequences. (पुलिस द्वारा अन्य अधिकारियों की गलत या अवैध गतिविधियों के संबंध में एक अघोषित नीति या उसे छिपाने का कृत्य)
 
 
• **Example: **Many reforms aim to dismantle the **blue code of silence** to ensure greater accountability within the police department.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the idiom **'Blue code of silence'** represents the concealment of illicit activities within the police force.

Therefore, the correct answer is- **An unspoken policy or concealment by police regarding the wrongdoing or illicit activity of other officers.**

**Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

__
 
• **A silence that unnerves one** (एक ऐसी चुप्पी जो किसी को घबरा दे): This refers to a quiet environment or situation that makes a person feel anxious, scared, or uneasy.
 
 
• **Example:** After the strange noise in the basement, there was **a silence that unnerves one**, making my heart race.
 
 
 
• **An absence of speech or sound that creates or communicates an especially effective or poignant message** (मौन की स्थिति जो एक विशेष रूप से प्रभावशाली या मर्मस्पर्शी संदेश देती है): Also known as eloquent silence, it is used to convey deep meaning without words.
 
 
• **Example:** When the **memorial** began, the **absence of speech** among the thousands of people communicated a powerful sense of shared grief.
 
 
 
• **A very tense, awkward, or uncomfortable atmosphere among a group of people** (लोगों के बीच एक बहुत ही तनावपूर्ण या असहज वातावरण): This describes a social situation filled with friction or embarrassment where no one knows what to say.
 
 
• **Example:** After the harsh criticism of the manager, there was **a very tense and uncomfortable atmosphere** in the meeting room.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **To think or act in accordance with set rules**.

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
He will have renovated the bungalow by next month.

options.text: The bungalow will have renovate by him by next month.
The bungalow will renovated by him by next month.
The bungalow will have been renovated by him by next month.
The bungalow has been renovated by him by next month.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The bungalow will have been renovated by him by next month.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The original sentence is in the **Future Perfect Tense**, which follows the active structure: **Subject + will + have + V3 (Past Participle) + Object**.

• To transform this into the **Passive Voice**, the grammatical rule dictates the following structure: **Object + will + have + been + V3 (Past Participle) + by + Subject**.

• The active subject **He** is replaced by the active object **The bungalow**, which becomes the grammatical subject in the passive construction.

• The pronoun **He** must be converted into its objective form, **him**, when placed after the preposition **by** as the agent of the action.

• The auxiliary phrase **will have been** is essential in the passive form to maintain the perfective aspect and the future timeline of the completion of the renovation.

• The main verb **renovated** is already in its **Past Participle** (V3) form and remains unchanged in the passive voice, paired with the auxiliary **been**.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Future Perfect Passive Construction**

• The use of **will have been** is mandatory for all subjects (singular or plural) in the **Future Perfect Passive** to indicate that an action will be completed relative to a future point.

• The word **been** serves as the critical marker that distinguishes the passive state from the **Active Future Perfect**, which would simply be **will have**.

• **Functional Use of Prepositions**

• In the passive sentence, the preposition **by** is used twice: first to identify the **agent** (the person performing the action, **him**) and second to denote the **time constraint** or deadline (**next month**).

• Maintaining the **time phrase** (by next month) at the end of the sentence ensures the context of the **Future Perfect Tense** is preserved accurately.

• **Pronoun Case Transformation**

• In English syntax, personal pronouns must change from the **nominative case** (He, She, I, They) to the **accusative/objective case** (him, her, me, them) when they shift from the subject position to the object/agent position in the passive voice.

</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
Were the musicians playing classical music at the concert?

options.text: Was classical music played at the concert by the musicians?
Was classical music being played at the concert by the musicians?
Has classical music been played at the concert by the musicians?
Is classical music being played at the concert by the musicians?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Was classical music being played at the concert by the musicians?**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence **Were the musicians playing classical music at the concert?** is an interrogative sentence in the **Past Continuous Tense**.
 
• In the **Active Voice**, the structure for this tense is: **Was/Were + Subject + Verb-ing + Object?**
 
• When converting to **Passive Voice**, the object of the active sentence **classical music** becomes the new subject. Since **classical music** is an uncountable and singular noun, the auxiliary verb **Was** is used.
 
• The specific rule for converting **Past Continuous** interrogative sentences into passive voice is: **Was/Were + Subject + being + Past Participle (V3) + by + Agent?**
 
• Following this rule, the verb **playing** is transformed into **being played** to maintain the continuous aspect of the action.
 
• The phrase **by the musicians** serves as the agent at the end of the sentence, completing the logical conversion while preserving the original meaning and tense.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• Understanding Tense Variations in Passive Voice:
 
 
• **Simple Past Tense**: Uses the structure **Was/Were + Subject + V3**. Option 1 follows this but fails to capture the continuous nature of the original verb.
 
• **Present Perfect Tense**: Uses **Has/Have + Subject + been + V3**. Option 3 is incorrect because it changes the tense from past to present perfect.
 
• **Present Continuous Tense**: Uses **Is/Am/Are + Subject + being + V3**. Option 4 is incorrect because it changes the timeline of the event from the past to the present.
 
• **Continuous Aspect**: In any continuous tense (present, past, or future), the addition of the word **being** is mandatory in the passive form to reflect that the action was ongoing.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
In the given question, a sentence is divided into four parts and given in the alternatives (A), (B), (C), and (D). There is an error in one part. Choose the alternative containing that part of the sentence that has the error. Choosing the alternative with the error will be the answer.
The only disadvantage with teaching is repeating the same curriculum again and again.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**disadvantage with teaching**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The segment **The only** acts as a specific **determiner phrase** that correctly limits the subject to a single negative aspect. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The phrase **disadvantage with teaching** contains a **prepositional error**; in English grammar, the noun **disadvantage** is typically followed by the preposition **of** when referring to an inherent quality or feature of an activity. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The part **is repeating the same** is grammatically sound, using the **linking verb** followed by a **gerund** (repeating) which serves as the **subject complement** to describe the disadvantage. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The concluding segment **curriculum again and again** correctly uses the object of the gerund and an **idiomatic adverbial phrase** to emphasize the repetitive nature of the task. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prepositional Collocations**:
 
 
• **Definition**: A **collocation** is a group of words that are frequently used together by native speakers.
 
• **Usage**: The noun **disadvantage** specifically pairs with **of** (e.g., the disadvantage **of** technology) or **to** (e.g., a disadvantage **to** the students). Using **with** in this context is non-standard.
 
 
 
• **Gerunds as Complements**:
 
 
• A **gerund** is a verb form ending in **-ing** that functions as a **noun**.
 
• In this sentence, **repeating** functions as a **predicate nominative**, providing more information about the subject (the disadvantage).
 
 
 
• **Emphasis in English**:
 
 
• Phrases like **again and again** or **time and again** are common **rhetorical devices** used to highlight the frequency or monotony of an action.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Select the correct alternative to fill in the blank with the correct preposition in the following sentence.

The police could not collect sufficient evidence ________ him to prove him guilty.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**against**'. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ 
• The preposition '**against**' is used to indicate **opposition**, **disagreement**, or in legal contexts, to indicate that someone is being **accused** of something. 
• The phrase '**evidence against someone**' is a standard expression used to describe facts or information that suggest a person is **guilty** of a crime or wrongdoing. 
• The sentence implies that the police were looking for proof of the person's **guilt**, making '**against**' the most appropriate fit. Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**. **Complete Sentence:** *"The police could not collect sufficient evidence **against**__ him to prove him guilty."* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 
• **Option 1: 'for'** is incorrect because evidence 'for' someone would typically mean **supportive evidence** or evidence in their favor, which contradicts the goal of proving them guilty. 
• **Option 2: 'about'** is incorrect because it is too **vague**; while we can have information about someone, evidence specifically linking them to a crime is usually 'against' them. 
• **Option 3: 'of'** is incorrect because we usually say '**evidence of a crime**' (e.g., evidence of theft), but not typically 'evidence of a person' in this context. </ul

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option which can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. In case Options A, B and C are not found suitable, choose Option D: "No Improvement Required."

The review panel concluded that the policy was __replete in inconsistencies and therefore required__ immediate revision.

options.text: replete with inconsistencies and therefore required
replete of inconsistencies and therefore requiring
replete by inconsistencies and therefore requires

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**replete with inconsistencies and therefore required**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The adjective **replete** is part of a specific prepositional collocation where it is almost exclusively followed by the preposition **with** to mean **filled** or **well-supplied**. Using **in**, **of**, or **by** in this context is grammatically incorrect.

• The sentence follows a **past tense** narrative structure, established by the main reporting verb **concluded** and the subsequent linking verb **was**.

• To maintain **tense consistency** and **parallelism** within the subordinate clause, the second action (governed by the same subject **policy**) must also be in the **simple past tense**. Therefore, **required** is the correct form to match **was**.

• Option 1 correctly combines the idiomatic preposition **with** and the past tense verb **required**, ensuring the sentence is both grammatically sound and logically consistent.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Understanding Prepositional Collocations:**

• **Replete with:** Formal term used for abundance or being full (e.g., a book **replete with** illustrations).

• **Full of:** A more common alternative, but specifically requires the preposition **of**.

• **Fraught with:** Typically used when something is filled with negative elements like **danger**, **difficulties**, or **risks**.

• **Abounding in/with:** Used to indicate that something exists in large numbers or amounts.

• **Tense Sequencing Rules:**

• When the **Principal Clause** is in the **Past Tense**, the **Subordinate Clause** must also be in the **Past Tense**, unless it expresses a universal truth or a habitual action.

• In this sentence, the need for **revision** is a specific past consequence of the **panel's** finding, necessitating the use of **required** over **requires** or **requiring**.

</ul

questions.question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1. I remember once out at St. Cloud. 

A. This Kzar is a great big yellow horse that looks like just nothing but run. 

B. I never saw such a horse. 

C. It was a big two hundred thousand franc race with seven entries and Kzar a big favourite. 

D. I went around to the paddock to see the horses with my old man and you never saw such horses. 

S2. He was being led around the paddocks with his head down and when he went by me I felt all hollow inside he was so beautiful.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph describes a specific memory of a horse race and the narrator’s reaction to a particular horse.
 
• **S1 is fixed** as the opening sentence: 
 
 
• 'I remember once out at **St. Cloud**.' - This sets the setting for the narrative.
 
 
 
• **Sentence C follows S1** because it provides the context for what was happening at St. Cloud:
 
 
• 'It was a big **two hundred thousand franc race** with seven entries and **Kzar** a big favourite.' - It defines the event and introduces the central subject, the horse named Kzar.
 
 
 
• **Sentence D is the next sentence** as it transitions from the race details to the narrator's direct experience:
 
 
• 'I went around to the **paddock** to see the horses with my **old man** and you never saw such horses.' - This establishes the physical location (paddock) and the act of observing the animals.
 
 
 
• **Sentence A follows D** as it focuses on the specific horse that was the favorite:
 
 
• 'This **Kzar** is a **great big yellow horse** that looks like just nothing but run.' - This gives a physical description of the horse mentioned in sentence C.
 
 
 
• **Sentence B follows A** to emphasize the narrator's awe:
 
 
• 'I **never saw such a horse**.' - This provides a personal emotive reaction to the physical description just given.
 
 
 
• **S2 is fixed** as the concluding sentence:
 
 
• 'He was being led around the **paddocks** with his head down and when he went by me I felt all hollow inside he was so **beautiful**.' - This perfectly complements the sequence by describing the horse's movement and the narrator's profound admiration.
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **CDAB**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

'I remember once out at **St. Cloud**. It was a big **two hundred thousand franc race** with seven entries and **Kzar** a big favourite. I went around to the **paddock** to see the horses with my **old man** and you never saw such horses. This **Kzar** is a **great big yellow horse** that looks like just nothing but run. I **never saw such a horse**. He was being led around the **paddocks** with his head down and when he went by me I felt all hollow inside he was so **beautiful**.'

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. If you feel Options A, B, or C do not improve the sentence, then choose Option D: "No improvement required."

They have __decided to for hire a cruise ship__ for their anniversary celebration.

options.text: decided for hiring a cruise ship
decided to hire a cruise ship

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**decided to hire a cruise ship**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence contains a **syntactic error** in the phrase 'to for hire'. In English grammar, an **infinitive marker** 'to' should be followed directly by the **base form** of the verb. The inclusion of the preposition 'for' between the infinitive marker and the verb creates a **redundancy** and violates standard **word order** rules.
 
• The verb **decide** is a **transitive verb** that typically requires a **to-infinitive** (to + verb) when it is used to express a choice or a resolution to perform a specific action. The structure **decided to hire** correctly follows this linguistic pattern, where 'to hire' serves as the **infinitive phrase** acting as the object of the decision.
 
• In this context, the term **hire** functions as a verb meaning to obtain the use of something for a fee. By removing the unnecessary preposition 'for', the sentence achieves **grammatical clarity** and logical flow, making 'decided to hire a cruise ship' the only syntactically sound replacement.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Infinitive vs. Gerund Collocations**:
 
 
• Specific verbs in English are followed by either an **infinitive** or a **gerund** (verb + -ing). Verbs like **decide**, **plan**, **agree**, and **hope** are strictly followed by infinitives.
 
• Option 1 ('decided for hiring') is incorrect because it uses a **prepositional gerund phrase** where a **to-infinitive** is required. The verb **decide** does not collocate with the preposition 'for' when followed by an action.
 
 
 
• **Prepositional Usage of For**:
 
 
• The preposition **for** is generally used to indicate **reason**, **purpose**, or **duration**. While one can 'decide for' a specific noun (e.g., 'decided for the blue car'), it is not used to introduce a verbal action in the same way an **infinitive** does.
 
• Option 3 ('decided for a cruise ship') removes the verb **hire** entirely, which changes the intended meaning of the sentence from the act of renting a vessel to simply choosing the vessel itself.
 
 
</ul
